text:
alex: Heads-up — PR #19987 touches the routing fallback and pulls in the new redis client. Integration job in eu-west is flaky and it's blocking merge. Is it better to split into a refactor + feature-flagged behavior or land behind a flag and enable post-maintenance? @maria @sam any preference?
ci-bot: integration/eu-west failed: `tests/integration/test-routing.py::TestRoute::test_fallback` — timeout on redis conn (attempt 3/3). Logs: `ConnectionError: timeout`
alex: My thinking: 1) split into two PRs (refactor only now; behavior + flag later) or 2) land single PR with `ff-routing-experimental` off by default and schedule canary after the maintenance window. Splitting keeps rebase surface small.
maria: prefer split + flag. If we land behavior behind a flag we still need telemetry to detect regressions. Can you add a simple metric: `route_experiment.p95_latency`?
jamie: QA: we can do a short smoke after canary, but our queue is full today. If this gets merged now it will get held during the 18:00 UTC deploy freeze and might sit unvalidated.
sam: Confirming deploy freeze at 18:00 UTC today for infra patch. If merged before freeze it will be held and not promoted. We can schedule a post-freeze canary at 02:00 UTC provided approvals are in by 01:30. If you want earlier validation you'll need to get a manual exception (not ideal).
alex: Good to know re: freeze. Splitting seems safest to avoid a long rebase window and to keep the new runtime change isolated. Would prefer to merge the refactor now with no behavioral change.
maria: I can add the feature flag scaffolding as a tiny follow-up PR and add the telemetry stub. If alex merges refactor-only we should be able to approve quickly.
ci-bot: rerun requested by alex — `./ci run integration --filter=eu-west`
ci-bot: rerun result: integration/eu-west flaky tests increased stability: test_fallback passed on attempt 1 (non-deterministic) — still marked flaky historically.
qa-bot: note: eu-west infra has intermittent redis timeouts during peak. For local repro, set `REDIS_TIMEOUT=2s` and run `pytest tests/integration/test-routing.py::TestRoute -k fallback`
sam: Plan: merge refactor PR now (no behavioral change). maria opens small PR for `ff-routing-experimental` + telemetry. We'll target the canary window 02:00 UTC after freeze; jamie will run smoke tests after canary. Alex — please tag me + @maria when both PRs are ready.
alex: Will open two PRs in ~15m and ping for reviews. Example flag YAML I'll add: ```yaml
feature_flags:
  ff-routing-experimental:
    default: false
    rollout: 0%
    owners: ["maria"]
    telemetry:
      - name: route_experiment.p95_latency
        type: histogram
```
jamie: adding :eyes: — can do quick smoke after canary, ping me once deploy-bot schedules it.
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary: PRs [19988,19989] -> 02:00 UTC (post-freeze). Canary window: 30m.
sam: Thanks all. Sounds like a safe path. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — I'll post the PR links when created.
